## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

 In the conclusion (*samodhāna*) of the tale preserved in the edition of Fausböll, the greedy monk is identified as having been a greedy crow (*lolakāko*) who died groaning at the scene, whereas the Bodhisatta was a pigeon (*pārāpato*) who abandoned the dwelling and flew elsewhere; upon hearing the exposition of the four truths, the greedy monk attained the fruit of non-returning (*anāgāmiphala*) [Fausböll 1879].
